class: A field's requirement decided from the whole page instead of from the field's own section and label
symptom: Found in the architecture review of 1 October: after the Meta fix (f086), one heading anywhere on a page reading 'account ... (optional)' made every password, passcode and one-time-code question on that page ignorable, and made account_state read the whole page as the application -- so a required sign-in or verification code in another section could be skipped and the run carried on past it.
site: Any portal that puts an optional account section on a page that also has a required credential
root_cause: page_agent.blockers and account_state.read_state each searched the page snapshot for an optional-account heading and, if found, let off every secret box, without asking which section each box sat in. The decision 'does this blank field need the owner?' existed in several places, each from page-wide evidence.
why_tests_missed: The Meta test page had only the optional account; no page put an optional account and a required sign-in together.
fix: field_requirements.py: fields() reads each control with the outline of headings above it; requirement() records required / optional / conditional / unknown with the evidence; requirement_for() takes the strictest when several fields share a label; needs_owner() is the one decision. page_agent.blockers skips only optional or conditional fields, logging the evidence (NOT NEEDED: ...); account_state treats a page as the application only when every secret box is inside an optional section, and otherwise counts only the boxes in use.
prevention: Give every field a section, a requirement status and the evidence for it when the page is read, and route every 'skip, fill or ask' through one function; never let a page-wide pattern excuse a field.
